m4.primaryBottleneck: observed fact: The listing is discovered mainly through Shopify App Store search/category browsing, is placed in the broad Analytics category, and the current headline emphasizes a specific pricing issue rather than the broader catalog-audit audience/job. interpretation: The most likely visibility bottleneck is search/category-match clarity at discovery, where merchants looking for catalog audit, product data quality, SKU, or merchandising issue tools may not immediately recognize the app as meant for them.
m4.competingExplanation: observed fact: The listing has 0 reviews and read-only safety is not prominent near the data access context. interpretation: Low trust after discovery could also suppress opens, so zero measured opens cannot be attributed to discovery alone.
m4.researchQuestion: hypothesis: Would a manual listing test that makes the audience and catalog-audit use case more explicit in the title/headline/above-the-fold copy improve qualified discovery and app opens from merchants searching for catalog quality problems, without changing app behavior?
notes: observed fact: reviewMode is exploratory_visibility_test, so sparse or zero metrics alone are not a reason to stop.
observed fact: app_opened_count, scan_started_count, and scan_completed_count are all 0, but Fly metrics are unavailable.
interpretation: With sparse metrics, the diagnosis should rely mainly on marketplace context and qualitative listing context rather than outcome proof.
observed fact: Promise clarity is strongest around below-cost pricing, compare-at price issues, duplicate SKUs, and missing SKUs.
observed fact: Audience specificity is implied but not explicit, and discovery-fit notes say the Analytics category may require clearer catalog-audit keywords.
interpretation: The listing may be too narrow in its visible framing for discovery even if the product solves a wider catalog-quality problem.
assumption: Shopify merchants often evaluate App Store results quickly using title, headline, category, and trust cues before opening an app listing.
observed fact: Trust friction exists too: 0 reviews and unclear read-only safety messaging near access expectations.

interpretation: Trust is a plausible secondary bottleneck, but the primary exploratory test should focus on discovery wording because the workflow asks for one likely visibility bottleneck hypothesis from listing and marketplace context.
observed fact: Listing observations are qualitative evidence only and do not prove causal impact.

m5.hypothesis: hypothesis: If the Shopify App Store listing is manually revised to make the audience and broader catalog-audit job more explicit above the fold, merchants browsing search/category results may more quickly recognize MerchGrid as a read-only catalog quality scanner rather than a narrowly priced-below-cost tool.
m5.recommendedRevision: Manually test a revised title/headline combination that keeps the below-cost proof point but adds clearer catalog-audit and merchant-fit language, such as shifting the headline from a single pricing issue to a broader framing like: 'Read-only catalog audit for Shopify merchants: find below-cost pricing, SKU gaps, duplicates, and compare-at issues before they hurt trust.'
m5.expectedSignal: interpretation: In sparse evidence conditions, the main signal to watch is whether more qualified merchants open the app listing and start a first scan after the copy revision, relative to the pre-change period. hypothesis: If discovery-match clarity is the main bottleneck, app opens should move before downstream scan completion does. observed fact: No outcome lift can be assumed from current evidence.
notes: observed fact: Current headline emphasizes priced-below-cost items, while other observed claims include duplicate SKUs, missing SKUs, and compare-at price issues.
observed fact: Audience specificity is implied but not explicit, and discovery-fit notes say clearer catalog-audit keywords may help in Shopify App Store search/category browsing.
observed fact: Trust friction also exists because there are 0 reviews and read-only safety is not prominent near data access context.
interpretation: This recommendation focuses on one exploratory discovery-language change only; it does not rule out trust as a competing explanation.
assumption: Merchants scanning Shopify App Store results use title/headline language to quickly judge whether an app fits their catalog-quality problem.

m6.baselinePeriod: Pre-change baseline from available sparse evidence snapshot captured by 2026-08-25, with current measured signals at 0 and no comparable historical traffic baseline available.
qualificationRequirements: Manual change only: revise one listing element at a time, starting with headline copy only.
Keep app behavior, pricing, category, screenshots, setup documentation, support links, and privacy links unchanged during the first test window.
Record the exact before-and-after headline text and the calendar date/time when the manual listing change goes live.
Use a fixed observation window after the change that is long enough to capture at least some listing traffic; if traffic remains at zero throughout the window, the result is not qualifying evidence.
Treat any improvement as exploratory unless it is accompanied by more qualified app opens and at least one scan start.
Do not attribute any movement to the headline test if other marketplace-facing changes occur during the same observation window.
If later instrumentation allows, segment for qualified traffic where possible so low-intent opens are not mistaken for better discovery match.
Human approval and manual marketplace edit are required before measurement.
Later evidence must be compared as exploratory and low confidence.
m6.expectedSupportingSignal: After a manual headline-only revision that makes catalog-audit audience fit clearer while preserving the existing pricing proof point, app_opened_count should increase first, followed by scan_started_count. A stronger supporting signal is more app opens with at least one resulting scan start and no corresponding rise in scan_failed_count.
m6.expectedWeakeningSignal: Little or no change in app_opened_count and scan_started_count after the headline-only test window, or more opens without any scan starts, would weaken the discovery-clarity hypothesis and make trust or post-open friction more plausible competing explanations.
m6.inconclusiveCondition: The test is inconclusive if marketplace traffic remains effectively zero, if measurement remains unavailable or too sparse to observe pre/post differences, or if multiple listing elements are changed during the same period so the effect cannot be isolated.
contextToMonitor: Whether the listing still shows 0 reviews during the test window, because trust friction may suppress opens or starts independently of discovery wording.
Whether read-only safety messaging remains absent near the access-risk context, because that could limit conversion from open to scan even if discovery improves.
Any Shopify App Store seasonality, placement shifts, or external promotion that could change exposure independently of the tested headline.
Whether the current title, category, screenshots, pricing label, and setup documentation remain unchanged so the test stays interpretable.
Any qualitative owner notes about merchant reactions or support questions after the copy change, especially questions about safety, access, or what happens after install.
